name: Positron annihilation and gamma detection
summary: Positron annihilation to two 511 keV photons is the basis of PET and of the Galactic 511 keV line, whose positron sources (compact binaries, supernovae, dark matter) remain debated.
breaks: The Galactic line's origin is unresolved; PET uses controlled β+ emitters.

name: Warm dense matter as strongly coupled plasma
summary: In warm dense matter the ions have Γ of order 1 or more and the electrons are partially degenerate (θ~1). OCP and Yukawa models, benchmarked on dusty plasmas, apply to the ion component only.

name: Burning-plasma physics across confinement schemes
summary: Both ICF and MCF aim at burning plasmas dominated by alpha heating, with a Lawson-type ignition condition. ICF uses a ρR criterion with hydrodynamic confinement; MCF uses nTτ_E with magnetic confinement.
breaks: ICF burn lasts about 100 ps and is limited by hydrodynamic disassembly. MCF burn is quasi-steady and limited by transport, MHD stability and exhaust.

name: Ponderomotive force in wakefields
summary: The ponderomotive force of a laser pulse expels electrons and excites the wake. Relativistic self-focusing and channeling guide the pulse.

name: Adiabatic invariants and magnetic focusing
summary: Gyration, mirror trapping and adiabatic invariants in plasma map onto betatron motion, Courant–Snyder invariants and magnetic confinement in storage rings and traps.
breaks: Accelerator lattices use alternating-gradient focusing with no plasma-style collective response.

name: Cyclotron isotope production for PET
summary: Medical cyclotrons produce PET isotopes via 18O(p,n)18F and 14N(p,α)11C, linking accelerator sources and targets to radiopharmaceutical supply.

name: Single-molecule FRET and spectroscopy
summary: smFRET applies Förster dipole-dipole energy transfer, E=1/(1+(r/R0)^6), and fluorescence photophysics from molecular spectroscopy to measure 2-10 nm distances and conformational dynamics in single molecules.

name: Molecular absorption and the greenhouse effect
summary: CO2, H2O and CH4 vibration-rotation bands (e.g. CO2 bending mode at 15 μm), with line strengths from spectroscopy databases such as HITRAN, set the opacity in line-by-line radiative transfer and hence greenhouse forcing.

name: Geodynamo and rotating convection
summary: Core convection in the geodynamo and atmospheric or oceanic convection are rotating, buoyancy-driven flows controlled by Rossby, Ekman and Rayleigh numbers with Taylor-column constraints.
breaks: Geodynamo has Lorentz forces, a much lower Ekman number (~1e-15) and no free surface or moist physics.

name: Caesium second and its optical redefinition
summary: The SI second is fixed by the Cs-133 hyperfine frequency 9 192 631 770 Hz, realized by caesium fountains at about 10⁻¹⁶. Optical lattice and ion clocks now reach about 10⁻¹⁸, so the CGPM is preparing to redefine the second with optical transitions.

name: Optical fibre solitons via NLS inverse scattering
summary: A pulse envelope in a Kerr fibre with anomalous dispersion obeys the focusing NLS. Zakharov–Shabat inverse scattering then predicts fundamental and higher-order solitons, as Hasegawa–Tappert did in 1973; Mollenauer observed them in 1980. The fundamental soliton needs peak power P₀=|β₂|/(γT₀²).

name: von Zeipel–Lidov–Kozai cycles in hierarchical triples
summary: Secular (double-averaged) perturbation by a distant third body exchanges inclination and eccentricity of an inner orbit above ~39.2°. This drives close binaries, hot Jupiters and merging compact binaries in triples.

name: Resonance chaos clears Kirkwood gaps
summary: Chaotic zones around Jupiter mean-motion resonances (Wisdom's 3:1 analysis) pump asteroid eccentricities until orbits cross Mars, clearing the Kirkwood gaps; secular resonance overlap also gives the inner planets ~5 Myr Lyapunov times (Laskar).

name: Solar convection zone and Schwarzschild criterion
summary: The outer ~30% of the Sun convects because its radiative temperature gradient exceeds the adiabatic one (Schwarzschild criterion, the inviscid buoyancy limit of Rayleigh–Bénard at enormous Ra). Granulation is the surface cells, and helioseismology locates the zone's base.

name: Phonon polaritons: light coupled to lattice oscillators
summary: Coupling the transverse photon to ionic TO-phonon oscillators (Huang 1951) gives two polariton branches with an avoided crossing. Between ω_T and ω_L, ε<0 opens a reststrahlen gap. The Lyddane–Sachs–Teller relation ties the LO–TO splitting to the static and high-frequency permittivities.

name: Incoherent Thomson scattering diagnostic of T_e and n_e
summary: Laser light Thomson-scattered by plasma electrons (scattering parameter α=1/kλ_D≪1) is Doppler-broadened by their thermal motion. The spectral width gives T_e and the absolute scattered power gives n_e, making Thomson scattering the reference profile diagnostic on tokamaks.

name: Replica method gives memory and perceptron capacities
summary: The replica method built for the SK spin glass computed the Hopfield storage capacity α_c≈0.138 (Amit, Gutfreund & Sompolinsky) and the Gardner volume capacity α_c=2 of the perceptron. Replica symmetry breaking and the cavity method now give phase diagrams of inference problems.

name: Landau collision integral: Boltzmann for Coulomb gases
summary: For long-range Coulomb scattering the Boltzmann collision integral is dominated by small-angle collisions and reduces to a Fokker–Planck form, Landau's 1936 collision operator, with the Coulomb logarithm cutting off at the Debye length. Lenard–Balescu adds dynamical screening. Spitzer conductivity and Braginskii transport follow by Chapman–Enskog.

name: Debye–Hückel as mean field; failure at strong coupling
summary: Debye shielding is the linearized Poisson–Boltzmann mean field, the same theory as Debye–Hückel electrolytes. It assumes a weak-coupling parameter Γ≪1. As Γ approaches and exceeds 1, correlations dominate: the pair correlation function develops liquid-like structure and the one-component plasma crystallizes near Γ≈175.

name: Nuclear liquid–gas transition
summary: Nucleon–nucleon forces, attractive at long range and repulsive at short range, give nuclear matter a van der Waals-like equation of state with spinodal and liquid–gas coexistence below a critical temperature of about 15–20 MeV. Plateaus in the multifragmentation caloric curve and Fisher-droplet fragment yields are read as its finite-size signatures.
breaks: Nuclei are finite, charged and two-component (isospin), and the collisions are transient, so the transition is smeared, Coulomb shifts it, and equilibrium is uncertain.

name: Clausius–Clapeyron and water-vapour feedback
summary: Clausius–Clapeyron fixes saturation vapour pressure growth at d ln e_s/dT=L/(R_vT²)≈6–7%/K near 288 K. At roughly constant relative humidity, this drives the water-vapour feedback, which about doubles warming, and the ~7%/K rise of extreme precipitation.

name: Clock comparisons search for ultralight scalar dark matter
summary: Ultralight scalar dark matter would make α and m_e oscillate at its Compton frequency. Comparisons of clocks with different sensitivity coefficients (for example Dy, Yb⁺/Sr, Cs/Rb) look for these oscillations and have set limits on the couplings.

name: Radiative multipoles: EM dipole vs GW mass/current quadrupole
summary: Thorne's (1980) multipole formalism expands gravitational radiation in mass and current multipoles, the analogues of electric and magnetic multipoles, using tensor spherical harmonics. Conservation removes the mass monopole and dipole and the current dipole, so radiation starts at ℓ=2; power ∝ (d^{ℓ+1}I_ℓ/dt^{ℓ+1})² in both.
map: P_{\rm EM}=\frac{|\ddot{\mathbf d}|^2}{6\pi\epsilon_0c^3}\ \leftrightarrow\ P_{\rm GW}=\frac{G}{5c^5}\langle\dddot Q_{ij}\dddot Q_{ij}\rangle

name: Holographic η/s versus the measured QGP viscosity
summary: The near-perfect fluidity of the QGP at RHIC and the LHC (hydrodynamic fits give η/s ≈ 1–2.5 × 1/4π) is compared with the holographic value ħ/4πk_B from black-brane horizons. Holography also models fast hydrodynamization via quasinormal-mode decay.
breaks: N=4 SYM is conformal and supersymmetric at infinite N and coupling, unlike QCD near T_c; the match is qualitative, and η/s ≥ 1/4π is not a true bound.

name: Optical clocks resolve gravitational redshift at millimetre scales
summary: Optical lattice clocks, with fractional uncertainty near 10⁻¹⁸, measure the redshift Δν/ν = gh/c² across height differences of centimetres. Bothwell et al. (2022) resolved it within a single millimetre-scale atomic sample. This tests local position invariance and enables relativistic geodesy.

name: GZK threshold as a probe of Lorentz violation
summary: Lorentz-violating dispersion shifts or removes the GZK photopion threshold, because Planck-suppressed terms are amplified at γ~10¹¹ (Coleman–Glashow). The observed ultra-high-energy flux suppression near 5×10¹⁹ eV therefore bounds such terms far below Planck-scale expectations, if the suppression is GZK.

name: Synchrotron radiation limits circular e⁺e⁻ colliders
summary: Larmor power from a charge on a circle grows as γ⁴/R², so energy loss per turn scales as E⁴/(m⁴R). This forced LEP's 27 km ring, sets FCC-ee's ~91 km circumference and RF budget, and makes muon colliders attractive: muons radiate (m_e/m_μ)⁴ ≈ 5×10⁻¹⁰ as much.

name: Proton-radius puzzle from muonic-hydrogen Lamb shift
summary: Muonic-hydrogen Lamb-shift spectroscopy (CREMA 2010) gave r_p ≈ 0.841 fm, about 4% (≈7σ) below the electronic-hydrogen and e–p scattering average. Later hydrogen spectroscopy and PRad scattering mostly support the small radius, which CODATA 2018 adopted. Some hydrogen results still disagree.

name: Coupled-cluster theory: from nuclei to molecules
summary: Coupled-cluster theory was introduced by Coester and Kümmel for nuclear matter (1958–60) and adopted by quantum chemistry (Čížek, Paldus). It now returns to nuclear structure as a polynomially scaling ab initio method reaching 208Pb.

name: Colour Debye screening in QGP
summary: Screening of colour charge in the quark–gluon plasma gives a Debye mass m_D~gT, mirroring electromagnetic Debye shielding; the QGP is also characterized by a coupling parameter and collective modes.
breaks: Non-Abelian gauge fields add gluon self-interaction, and confinement physics has no EM-plasma counterpart; screening is perturbative only at high T.
